run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation namespace was recreated at 23:38:29-23:38:46, so the authorized window contains only ~28 s of application traffic (first traces at 23:38:57.77). In that sampled traffic the request path was healthy: frontend server spans for HTTP GET /hotels and /recommendations carry http.status_code 200 at 2.4-4.5 ms and their dependency spans (search, geo, rate, profile, recommendation, reservation) carry no error tags; the rate service reported 83 requests received/83 completed, 0 rejected, 0 expired, queue depth 0. The one failing component observed inside the window is the reservation-cleanup path: ConfigMap hotel-reservation/reservation-cleanup-token is stuck Terminating (deletionTimestamp 23:38:46, finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup) because the cleanup-controller pod's finalizer-removal PATCH is rejected with HTTP 403 every 2 s from 23:38:47 onward, and the ClusterRole bound to its ServiceAccount (configmap-cleanup-controller) grants only get/list/watch on configmaps - no patch/update. That is the deepest cause the evidence supports. I found no evidence of an application-path outage, crash, OOM or latency escalation in the window; the mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate privilege-revocation scripts staged into the new mongodb ReplicaSets are a candidate that remains unproven because no authorization failure was observed.

The cleanup-controller container in pod hotel-reservation/cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-j6prq logs the same two-line failure every 2 seconds from 2026-11-23T23:38:47Z through 23:38:57Z: 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' followed by 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' (194 further such lines were emitted after the window ended).

ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller binds ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller to ServiceAccount cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation, and Deployment hotel-reservation/cleanup-controller runs 'python /controller/controller.py' with that ServiceAccount and the cleanup-controller-script ConfigMap mounted at /controller.

A pod-template change inside the window created new ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 (23:38:33Z) and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 (23:38:34Z) that add a /scripts volume from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, while the previous ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf were scaled to 0 replicas.

ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate contain scripts that revoke the readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db from MongoDB user 'admin' (revoke-admin-*-mongo.sh) and scripts that drop the MongoDB 'admin' user (remove-admin-mongo.sh), i.e. they are privilege-revocation fault tools mounted, but not automatically executed, by the mongodb pods.

Blackbox probes at 2026-11-23T23:38:58Z report probe_success=0 with probe_http_status_code=0 and no established IP for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo:8083, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, search:8082, user:8086 and for the ingress probe of http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels, while profile:8081 and reservation:8087 report probe_success=1; these probe series hold exactly one sample in the 24-hour window.

The primary fault is the missing authorization on the cleanup path: ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller does not grant patch/update on configmaps, so the cleanup-controller's finalizer-removal PATCH is denied (HTTP 403) and ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token can never finish terminating; the reservation-cleanup bookkeeping is therefore permanently blocked, although no user-facing request error was observed.

A second candidate remains open: a MongoDB privilege-revocation fault against geo-db and/or rate-db was staged at 23:38:33-34 by mounting failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate into the new mongodb ReplicaSets; I could not observe the scripts being executed and saw no authorization failure in the window, so I cannot confirm or exclude that this fault was applied.

The probe_success=0 readings do not match the served traffic in the same window: at 23:38:57.7-57.98Z the frontend returned http.status_code=200 for /hotels and /recommendations, so I do not treat the single blackbox sample at 23:38:58Z as evidence that those services were down.

Rate-service queue saturation / throttling as the cause is rejected for the sampled window: at 23:38:58Z queue depth was 0, in-flight 0, rejected 0, expired 0, received equalled completed at 83, the backend QPS limit was 500, and observed frontend latencies were <=4.5 ms.
Pod crash / OOMKilled as the cause is rejected: no hotel-reservation container has a restart, a waiting reason or a lastState.terminated reason, and all 20 pods are Ready.

gaps: No baseline exists inside the authorized window: namespace hotel-reservation was created 2026-11-23T23:38:29Z, every pod started 23:38:30-23:38:44Z, the first Jaeger traces are at 23:38:57.77Z and the rate/search/blackbox series each hold one sample, so no latency or error-rate trend can be established and no pre-incident behaviour can be compared.

Data after the window end (2026-11-23T23:38:58Z) is not queryable: the cleanup-controller emitted 194 further error lines after the window, and alert rule state at ~23:40Z showed HighRequestRate pending for frontend, search, reservation, rate and profile - these are outside the window and are not used as incident evidence.

Search-service golden signals could not be read inside the window: search_rate_attempts_total, search_rate_failures_total, search_rate_successes_total, search_rate_timeouts_total and search_requests_total exist as metric names but an instant query for them at 23:38:58Z returned no data, so search-to-rate retry/timeout behaviour is unobserved.

Whether the revoke-admin-geo / revoke-admin-rate scripts were actually executed cannot be determined from the available tools (no command history; kube exec is not available). A log filter of mongodb-geo for 'not authorized|Authentication failed|Unauthorized' returned no lines, but that view has status no_data and therefore proves nothing about absence.

Secrets are unreadable: the data of ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token (key cleanup-token, source reservation-maintenance) was credential-redacted, so whether that token ties the stuck cleanup to the reservation service cannot be verified.

No evidence observed that hotel reservation placement or availability checking is affected by the stuck ConfigMap; downstream/customer impact is unverified and would need a longer observation of reservation requests and the reservation service's cleanup/maintenance behaviour.

The blackbox probe configuration (modules/expected codes) is unknown, so the meaning of probe_success=0 for 6 of 8 services at 23:38:58Z, while the same services were serving traffic, could not be resolved.
next_steps: Review the ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller contract and grant the cleanup-controller ServiceAccount patch (or update) on configmaps so it can remove the cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup finalizer from Terminating ConfigMaps.
Inspect the reservation service's maintenance/cleanup logic to determine whether it depends on reservation-cleanup-token and whether a permanently Terminating ConfigMap blocks reservation cleanup.

Collect a longer baseline once the load generator has ramped (HighRequestRate was pending for five hotel-reservation services after the window) and compare p95 latency and error rate per service before declaring the application path healthy.
Verify with a database client whether the MongoDB 'admin' user still holds readWrite on geo-db and rate-db, since the failure-admin-* revoke scripts are now mounted in the running mongodb pods.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
view.incomplete_reason: limit: the newest 80 of 212 matching lines are shown

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

NAMESPACE = "hotel-reservation"
FINALIZER = "cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup"
LABEL_SELECTOR = "app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup"
TOKEN_FILE = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
CA_FILE = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
API_SERVER = (
    f"https://{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST']}:"
    f"{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT_HTTPS']}"
)
TLS_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=CA_FILE)


def api_request(method, path, payload=None):
    data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    headers = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    if payload is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/merge-patch+json"
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{API_SERVER}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL],
        method=method,
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=TLS_CONTEXT, timeout=10) as response:
        raw = response.read()
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}


def reconcile():
    selector = urllib.parse.quote(LABEL_SELECTOR, safe="")
    response = api_request(
        "GET",
        f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps?labelSelector={selector}",
    )
    for configmap in response.get("items", []):
        metadata = configmap.get("metadata", {})
        finalizers = metadata.get("finalizers", [])
        if not metadata.get("deletionTimestamp") or FINALIZER not in finalizers:
            continue

        name = metadata["name"]
        remaining = [item for item in finalizers if item != FINALIZER]
        print(
            f"ConfigMap {name} is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup",
            flush=True,
        )
        encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(name, safe="")
        api_request(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps/{encoded_name}",
            {"metadata": {"finalizers": remaining}},
        )
        print(f"ConfigMap {name} cleanup completed", flush=True)


print(f"cleanup-controller starting namespace={NAMESPACE}", flush=True)
while True:
    try:
        reconcile()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        if error.code == 403:
            print(
                "cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: "

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"
